text:
The evidence doesn't establish deforestation, but it does show tree-cover loss.

Hansen/UMD mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021, roughly 2.2% of the 3,643.5 ha property. The JRC 2020 map agrees that the area was forest at the end of 2020 (98% agreement), and later years of the series were observed, so the loss is corroborated.

The forest map shows that most of the affected area (68.1 ha) was planted pine (*Pinus elliottii* and *Pinus taeda*). None was native forest, and 13.2 ha fell outside mapped forest. Hansen's loss measure includes any stand replacement, such as harvesting a plantation, so this pattern could be routine plantation cutting. The data can't tell us.

The data also doesn't show the cause, legality, who was responsible, or any compliance status. Separately, another 37.3 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was not counted as an event.

Confirming deforestation would require evidence of land-use change after the loss, such as what replaced the trees.
